threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, close calendar, and responsibilities for the upgraded process.

messages.text: Sharing the first draft of the quarter-end close calendar and checklist for the Quarter-End Close and Tax Compliance Process Upgrade project_pack_ref: quarter-close-upgrade. This is the backbone for T1 and will feed into the roles playbook under T11. The draft is in A1 and I mapped activities by day 1 to 7, with owners by role. Key points: day 1 pre-close reconciliations and cut-off confirmations, days 2 to 4 journals and reviews, day 5 tax and depreciation checks, day 6 draft statements, day 7 final review and sign-off. Please review whether the 7 business day target is realistic and if the responsibilities per step match how we actually work. I will consolidate feedback into A1 and A5 before we lock anything.

Thanks for sharing. I walked through A1 and the mapping looks close to what we did last quarter, but more structured. A couple of observations: 1 the tax and depreciation checks on day 5 depend on having all high-risk journals posted and reviewed earlier. Maybe we should explicitly link those to the peer review work under T7, even if that task sits in another thread. 2 For the playbook in A5, can we add a column for backup owner per activity so we are covered if someone is out during close. On the 7 day target, I think it is achievable if departments send supporting docs on time, but we will need clear cut-off rules and escalation paths in T11.

I went line by line through the checklist in A1. From the bookkeeping side, the main pressure points are: accruals and provisions journals, and collecting certificates from departments. Right now, some of those are on day 3 and 4. If we want to stay within 7 days, I suggest we move the request for supporting documents earlier as a pre-close activity, even if the actual posting stays in the 7 day window. That would also align with the documentation standards we are defining under T5. For responsibilities, I see bookkeeper as owner for most journals, but for complex tax and depreciation entries, I would expect shared responsibility with financial manager, especially where tax legislation is involved.

I have a question on the calendar in A1. For day 2 you listed general ledger reconciliations and intercompany checks. In practice, we sometimes start those before quarter-end using estimates. Do you want us to keep that flexibility, or should we strictly follow the day by day order. Also, for T1, are we including the pre-close reminders to departments in the same checklist, or will that sit in a separate reminder schedule. It would help me if the responsibilities in A5 clearly show who sends which reminder and by when.

From my side, the 7 day target seems tight but manageable if we formalise the pre-close work. I agree with moving document collection earlier, as suggested. For T11, I can help draft the RACI in A5 based on how we handled last year end close. One concern: the external tax advisor only has four review slots. Should we block one of those in the calendar on day 5 or 6, and mark it clearly in A1 so we do not overbook that day with other heavy tasks.

Good points. I will update A1 to show explicit dependency between high-risk journals and the tax and depreciation checks, and reference the peer review process from T7. For A5, adding a backup owner column makes sense, I will include that in the T11 scope. On the 7 day target, I hear general agreement that it is possible but only if we manage pre-close work and department submissions better. I will draft a pre-close section in the checklist and share for review before we confirm D1.

Agree on shifting document requests earlier. I will add a pre-close phase in A1, say day minus 3 to day 0, where we send reminders and collect certificates, aligned with the standards from T5. For complex tax and depreciation entries, we can define joint responsibility: bookkeeper prepares, financial manager reviews and approves. I will reflect that split in A5 under T11 so it is clear who does what.

On the reconciliations, I do not want to block useful early work. Let us keep the calendar in A1 as the latest completion date for each activity, but we can note that some reconciliations may start earlier with estimates. For T1, I suggest we keep pre-close reminders in the same checklist so we have a single view of all actions. In A5, we will specify that bookkeepers send reminders for their areas, and I will own the escalation path if departments are late.

On the tax advisor slots, I recommend we block one slot around day 5 focused on complex tax positions from T8, and keep day 6 a bit lighter on internal reviews so we can adjust if needed. In A1, we can mark that slot as external dependency and in A5 we can assign preparation of the list of items to financial manager, with support from bookkeepers for data extraction.

One more detail for A1 and A5. For the cut-off rules, can we document clearly when we stop accepting adjustments that impact tax, versus operational corrections that can wait until next period. That will help us avoid last minute changes that complicate T3 and T8. Maybe in T11 we add a short section on cut-off principles and who can approve exceptions.

Agree with keeping everything in one checklist. For T1, I can help refine the wording of the pre-close tasks in A1 so they are easy to follow. For responsibilities in A5, I suggest we also indicate which tasks require peer review or second pair of eyes, even if the detailed checklist for that sits in another artifact. That will make the playbook more practical for new team members.

With the pre-close phase and clearer cut-off rules, I am comfortable with the 7 day target. The only area I am still unsure about is workload on day 3 and 4 for journals. Maybe we can spread some of the smaller recurring entries to day 2 if reconciliations finish early. Not a blocker, but worth noting in A1 so we can adjust during the trial run under T10.

I will add a cut-off section in A1 and A5 as part of T11, distinguishing between tax sensitive adjustments and operational corrections. For now, proposal is: tax impacting adjustments allowed up to end of day 4 with my approval, after that only corrections that do not change tax or key metrics. I will also mark in the checklist which tasks are candidates for peer review, so we can align with the separate peer review checklist later.

Spreading smaller recurring entries earlier makes sense. We can tag them in A1 as flexible within days 2 to 4, and during the trial run for T10 we will see how that impacts timings. As long as the main dependencies for tax and statements are respected, this should not create issues.

I have now updated A1 and A5 based on the discussion: added pre-close phase for document collection and reminders, marked the external tax advisor slot linked to T8, clarified cut-off rules, added backup owners and peer review flags, and aligned responsibilities for complex tax and depreciation entries. Given these changes, I would like to formally confirm that we are aiming for completion of the quarter-end close within 7 business days and that the responsibilities per activity in A5 under T11 are acceptable. If there are no strong objections, I will record this as our agreed calendar and scope for D1 and D2.

I reviewed the latest A1 and A5. The 7 day calendar with the added pre-close tasks looks workable, and the split of responsibilities, including joint work on complex entries, is clear enough for me. No objections from my side to locking in D1 and D2.
Same here, I am aligned with the 7 day target and the responsibilities in A5. The explicit dependencies and cut-off rules will help us stay on track. Happy to proceed with D1 and D2 as stated.

Confirmed from my side as well. The calendar in A1 and the playbook structure in A5 give enough guidance, and we can fine tune details during the trial run. No further comments before we close D1 and D2.

threads.thread_goal: Define standards for journal entries and supporting documentation.

messages.text: Kicking off the standards discussion for journal entries and documentation. I have drafted templates for recurring journals under T2 and a first version of documentation and attachment standards under T5. The templates cover payroll, depreciation, accruals, and provisions, with required fields and example descriptions. For documentation, A4 outlines which certificates or supporting files are needed by transaction type, plus naming and storage rules. I also linked the peer review checklist from A7 so we can align on how to flag high-risk entries for T7. Please review and comment before we agree on what becomes mandatory from next close.

I went through the templates in T2. The structure is solid, especially the separate fields for narrative and reference to source documents. One suggestion: for tax sensitive entries, could we add a field to capture the specific tax rule or article, so we can trace back to legislation during audits. On A4, the list of required documents by transaction type is clear, but I wonder if we should differentiate between mandatory certificates and nice to have documents, to avoid overloading the process.

On A4, I have a question about storage conventions. You propose a folder structure by year, quarter, and transaction type. In practice, we sometimes store certificates by department. Should we standardise fully on the new structure, or allow a hybrid where departments keep their own copies as long as we have a central version following A4. For A7, the peer review checklist looks good, but I am not sure how we decide which entries are high-risk under T7.

I like the consistency in the T2 templates. For provisions, could we add a field for expected reversal date or condition, so we can track when to release them. That would help when preparing the financial statements. On documentation, A4 mentions random file audits. Maybe we should specify a minimum sample per quarter so expectations are clear.

Thanks for pulling this together. From a control perspective, I want to make sure the templates under T2 and the standards in A4 are enough to satisfy audit and tax requirements without slowing us down too much. I am not fully sure how strict we need to be on naming conventions and whether auditors expect a specific pattern. I will check with our external auditor contact and confirm if the proposed A4 structure is acceptable before we finalise D3 and D4.

Good call on tax sensitive entries. We can add a field in the T2 templates called tax reference, where we capture the relevant rule or internal note. That will also help when we update the tax workbook in A2. On A4, I suggest we keep the list focused on mandatory documents only, and add an optional column for recommended extras. That way we do not create unnecessary work but still encourage good practice.

For storage, I would standardise on the central structure in A4 as the official record, but departments can keep their own copies if they want. We just need to be clear that for audits we rely on the central repository. On high-risk criteria for T7, my proposal is: entries above a materiality threshold, anything impacting tax, manual adjustments to depreciation, and unusual or one-off transactions. We can document these criteria in A7 so everyone applies them consistently.

Agree on provisions. I will add expected reversal date or condition to the T2 template and a reminder in A4 that supporting documentation should include the basis for the estimate. For random file audits, we can set a minimum of, say, 10 entries per quarter or 5 percent of total high-risk entries, whichever is higher. I will note that in A4 so it is transparent.

The proposed high-risk criteria in A7 make sense to me. Maybe we should also include entries involving manual overrides of system calculations, for example depreciation adjustments that bypass A3. That would ensure we capture anything that could create inconsistencies with the fixed asset schedule.

On the random file audits, would we rotate responsibility among bookkeepers or have one person own it. A4 mentions that evidence of review should be stored with the journal entry. I just want to be sure we do not miss documenting who performed the audit and when.

The tax reference field will be very helpful when we prepare the compliance review under T12. We can quickly see which entries are tax relevant and cross check them against the tax workbook in A2. Maybe we should also add a simple yes or no flag for tax impact in the T2 templates to make filtering easier.

I spoke briefly with our audit contact. They are fine with any naming convention as long as it is consistent and traceable, and they like the idea of linking entries to tax references and depreciation schedules. So A4 as proposed, with the tweaks discussed here, should be acceptable. From my side, I am comfortable making the T2 templates mandatory for recurring entries from next close, and adopting A4 and A7 as our standard for documentation and peer review, provided everyone here is aligned.

Good addition. I will update A7 to include manual overrides of system calculations as high-risk, and reference A3 and T4 where relevant. I will also clarify in A4 that the random file audit log should record who performed the check and the date, and that this log is stored alongside the journal entry documentation.

On ownership of random file audits, I suggest we rotate among bookkeepers but keep a simple tracker in A4 showing who is assigned each quarter. That spreads the workload and keeps everyone familiar with the standards. The evidence of review will sit with each entry, as you mentioned.

I am aligned with making the T2 templates mandatory for recurring entries and adopting A4 and A7 as our standards. The extra tax reference and tax impact flag will help a lot during reviews. No objections to D3 and D4 from my side.
Agreed as well. The standards in A4 and the peer review checklist in A7 are clear enough for me to follow, and the templates under T2 will reduce back and forth. Happy to proceed with D3 and D4.
Confirmed from my side too. I will start using the new templates for any test entries we do before quarter-end, so we can iron out small issues early. No further comments before we lock D3 and D4.

threads.thread_goal: Validate tax and depreciation schedules and align with tax advisor.

messages.text: I have uploaded the updated tax calculation workbook in A2 and the latest fixed asset depreciation schedule in A3 for this quarter. These are the outputs of T3 and T4. Tax rates and thresholds have been updated based on the latest legislation, and I ran sample calculations against prior quarter figures. For depreciation, all active assets are listed with cost, life, and method, and the totals reconcile to the general ledger. Before we book anything, I need your review on both files and input on any edge cases we should raise with the tax advisor under T8. Once we are comfortable, we can sign off D5 for the tax workbook and D6 for the depreciation schedule.

I reviewed A3 first. The asset list looks complete and the depreciation methods match our policy summary. I spot checked a few assets and the quarterly depreciation ties to the general ledger. One thing to flag: there are a couple of assets with remaining useful life of less than one year but still using straight line over the original term. We might want to consider whether an adjustment is needed or at least document the rationale. For A2, I checked the main tax rates and they align with the latest guidance I have. I did not see a separate tab for deferred tax; is that intentional for this quarter.

On A2, I walked through the reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable profit. The adjustments for depreciation, provisions, and non-deductible expenses look reasonable. However, I noticed that the new tax incentive for certain assets is not explicitly shown. Do we plan to apply it this quarter, and if so, should we add a separate line in the workbook. For A3, I agree with the reconciliation, but I would like to confirm how we are handling fully depreciated assets that are still in use, just to be sure we are consistent with prior quarters.

I have a question on the link between A3 and the journal entries we will post. For T4, will we use a standard template from T2 for the depreciation journal, or is there a separate format. I want to make sure the amounts we post match the schedule exactly and that we attach the right extract from A3 as documentation.

From the financial statements angle, the totals in A2 and A3 look consistent with what we expect for the quarter. I compared the effective tax rate in A2 with last quarter and the variance is mainly due to the change in non-deductible expenses, which is explained in the notes. For depreciation, the movement in net book value aligns with the capex and disposals we recorded. I think the potential tax incentive mentioned should be clarified with the tax advisor under T8 before we finalise D5.

Thanks for the checks. On the assets with short remaining life, I followed the original schedule, but you are right that we should at least document the rationale. I will add a note in A3 explaining that we are keeping the original pattern due to immaterial impact, unless the tax advisor suggests otherwise. Regarding deferred tax in A2, I did not include a separate tab because our exposure is small, but I can add a simple summary tab so we have a complete view.

On the new tax incentive, I was not fully sure how it applies to our assets, so I left it out of A2 for now. We should definitely raise this in the T8 discussion with the tax advisor. I will prepare a list of potentially eligible assets from A3 and add a separate section in A2 to model the impact, so we can adjust after the advisor confirms. For fully depreciated assets still in use, we are keeping them at zero net book value but tracking them in the schedule for control purposes, consistent with prior quarters.

For T4, we should definitely use the standard journal template from T2 for depreciation. That way we can link each journal line back to the relevant section of A3 and keep documentation consistent with A4. I can help set up a simple export from A3 that matches the template layout, so posting is straightforward and we avoid manual retyping.

Adding a deferred tax summary tab in A2 is a good idea, even if the amounts are small. It will help during the compliance review and when we explain movements to auditors. For the short life assets in A3, I agree that documenting the rationale is enough if the impact is immaterial, but we should still flag them as items to mention in the T8 call so the tax advisor is aware.

Thanks, that helps. Once the export from A3 is ready, I will test posting a sample depreciation journal using the T2 template and check that the totals match. I will also make sure we attach the relevant A3 extract as per A4, so we are ready for peer review under A7 if needed.

For the tax incentive, I can help prepare the list of potentially eligible assets from A3 and draft the questions for the T8 meeting. It would be useful to include both the accounting and tax impact scenarios in A2, so we can quickly update once we get confirmation. That will also make it easier to explain any changes in the effective tax rate later.

Thanks for checking the overall consistency. Given the feedback so far, I will: add a deferred tax summary tab in A2, document the rationale for short life assets in A3, prepare a list of potentially eligible assets for the tax incentive, and include these points in the T8 agenda. Once those updates are in place, I think we can consider A2 and A3 ready for sign-off, subject to any final comments.

With those adjustments, I am comfortable treating A3 as final for this quarter, and using it as the basis for posting depreciation under T4. For A2, as long as the deferred tax summary and the incentive scenario are added, I am fine to proceed and adjust later if the tax advisor suggests changes. No further issues from my side before we confirm D5 and D6.

I agree. Once the extra tabs and notes are in A2 and A3, I see no blockers. We can highlight the incentive and short life assets in the T8 discussion, but that should not stop us from signing off D5 and D6 for internal purposes.

From my side, the link between A3 and the journals is clear now, and the reconciliations in A2 look fine. I am ok with treating both as final for this quarter, subject to any minor tweaks after the T8 call. No objections to D5 and D6.

Same here. The schedules in A2 and A3 are consistent with the financials we expect, and the open points are clearly identified for T8. I support signing off D5 and D6 now and documenting any later adjustments through the normal close process.

threads.thread_goal: Run and debrief the trial close using the new checklist.

messages.text: I have completed the trial run of the new close checklist in A1 using last month data, as part of T10. I recorded timings for each step and logged issues and bottlenecks in A8. Overall, we finished the simulated close in 6 business days, but that was without real department delays. The main bottlenecks were: collecting certificates from two departments, peer review of high-risk entries, and final tax reconciliation. I have added comments in A8 with suggestions, but I would like everyone to review and see what we should adjust in the checklist before quarter-end.

Thanks for running the trial. Looking at A8, I see that document collection still caused delays even in a controlled test. For A1, I suggest we move the first reminder to departments earlier and add a second reminder with escalation if documents are not received by the pre-close cut-off. On peer review, the time spent was higher than expected. Maybe we should refine the high-risk criteria in A7 or batch reviews to specific time slots instead of ad hoc checks.

I reviewed the timings in A8. The tax reconciliation step took longer mainly because we had to cross check several entries without clear tax references. With the new T2 templates and A4 standards, that should improve, but I still think we should allocate a fixed time window in A1 for tax review, ideally after most high-risk entries are posted and reviewed. Also, for T12, we might want to capture not only exceptions but also which steps consistently run close to the deadline.

From the trial, I noticed that the final review of the draft statements, which links to A6, was squeezed into the last day. In A1, maybe we should bring some of that analysis earlier, for example preliminary variance checks once most journals are posted. That would reduce pressure on the last day and give us more time to react if something looks off.

Thanks for documenting everything in A8. It is encouraging that the trial finished in 6 days, but we should not assume real close will be that smooth. I agree we need to tweak A1 based on these findings. My initial thoughts: strengthen pre-close reminders and escalation, schedule dedicated peer review slots, and bring forward some of the variance analysis linked to T6. Let us discuss specific changes and then we can record D7 on which adjustments we are making to the checklist.

On document collection, during the trial I simulated one reminder only, which is why delays showed up clearly in A8. I agree that adding a second reminder and escalation in A1 would help. For peer review, I applied the full high-risk criteria from A7, which may have been conservative. Maybe we can refine thresholds or group similar entries for review to save time.

Makes sense. I propose we adjust A7 so that only entries above a certain amount or with complex tax impact require full peer review, while smaller recurring entries can be sampled. In A1, we can then block two specific time windows for peer review on days 3 and 4, instead of spreading it across the whole period. That should reduce context switching and improve throughput.

Agree on allocating a fixed tax review window. In A1, we could set a dedicated block on day 5 for tax reconciliation, after most high-risk entries have been reviewed. With the new tax reference field in T2 and the standards in A4, that should be more efficient than what we saw in the trial. For T12, I can help refine the way we capture near-deadline steps so we can track trends over several closes.

On bringing variance analysis earlier, we could add a preliminary review step in A1 on day 5 or 6, where we run a draft A6 package with current data. That would not be final, but it would highlight any unusual movements. Then the last day would focus on confirming numbers rather than discovering surprises.

I like the idea of batching peer reviews and tightening the criteria in A7. We just need to be careful not to miss material items. Let us document the new thresholds clearly and monitor during the next close. For A1, I will add two peer review blocks on days 3 and 4, and a dedicated tax review block on day 5 as suggested. These changes should address two of the main bottlenecks from A8.

That works for me. During the trial, tax review overlapped with other tasks, which made it harder to focus. A dedicated block in A1 should help. For T12, I will add a column in A8 to mark steps that finished within a few hours of the deadline, so we can see which ones are consistently tight.

Agreed on monitoring. After the first real close with the new setup, we can revisit A7 and A8 to see if the thresholds are appropriate. For now, the adjustments you described in A1 should be enough to reduce the trial bottlenecks without adding too much complexity.

If we add a preliminary A6 run on day 5 or 6, we should also note in A8 whether that step actually helps catch issues earlier. I can take responsibility for running that draft package during the first real close and logging any findings in T12.

Summarising the adjustments we are proposing to the checklist in A1 based on the T10 trial and A8 findings: 1 add a second department reminder and explicit escalation path in the pre-close phase, 2 schedule two dedicated peer review blocks on days 3 and 4 and refine high-risk criteria in A7, 3 allocate a fixed tax review window on day 5, and 4 introduce a preliminary draft A6 run on day 5 or 6 for early variance analysis. If everyone agrees, I will update A1 and A7 accordingly and record D7 that these changes are adopted for the upcoming quarter-end close.

The summary matches my understanding of the changes. These adjustments should address the main bottlenecks we saw in A8 without changing the overall 7 day target. I support updating A1 and A7 as described and proceeding with D7.
Aligned from my side as well. The refined peer review approach and clearer scheduling in A1 should make the process smoother. Happy to move forward with D7.
Confirmed. The preliminary A6 run and the dedicated review windows will help us manage the workload better. No further comments before we lock D7.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare final quarter-end package and confirm readiness for auditors.

messages.text: I have posted the draft quarter-end financial statements package in A6, which is the main deliverable for T6. It includes the balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, and key variance analysis versus prior quarter. I also linked the latest compliance review log in A8 and the updated checklist completion status. Before we send anything to the external auditor, I need your review on the numbers, explanations, and whether the supporting documentation is complete according to A4. Once we are comfortable, we can approve D8 and treat this package as ready for submission.

I reviewed A6 focusing on the variance analysis. The main movements in revenue and operating expenses are well explained, and the effective tax rate reconciles to A2. One area that might need a clearer note is the increase in provisions; we should tie that explanation back to the new T2 template fields and the documentation in A4. From a structure point of view, the package looks ready, but I would like to confirm that all high-risk entries have peer review evidence attached as per A7 before we sign off D8.

On the documentation side, I sampled a set of entries linked to the larger variances in A6 and checked them against A4 and A8. Most of them have the correct certificates and naming conventions. I did find a few cases where the tax reference field in the T2 template was left blank even though the entry affects tax. We should fix those before sending the package, as auditors may ask for the underlying rationale.

I checked the tax related notes in A6 against the tax workbook in A2. The numbers tie, and the explanation of the incentive treatment matches what we agreed with the tax advisor under T8. For the compliance review in A8, I see a couple of minor exceptions still open, mainly late attachments that were added after the initial deadline. We should document the remediation clearly in T12 so auditors see that the issues were addressed.

From the bookkeeping perspective, the balances in A6 reconcile to the general ledger, and the depreciation and fixed asset movements match A3. I did not see any unexplained differences. My only question is whether we need an additional note on the fully depreciated assets still in use, or if the existing disclosure is enough.

Good catch on the provisions. I will expand the note in A6 to reference the updated T2 template fields and clarify the basis for the increase, linking back to the supporting documents listed in A4. On peer review evidence, I will ask that we run a quick check against A7 to confirm that all high-risk entries in the package have documented reviews before we finalise D8.

I can take care of the missing tax references in the T2 templates. I will go through the sample you flagged and any other tax impacting entries tied to major variances in A6, update the tax reference field, and ensure the documentation in A4 is complete. I will also confirm that peer review evidence is attached where required by A7.

For the open exceptions in A8, I will update T12 with a short remediation note for each, including when the missing attachments were added and any follow up with departments. That should make it clear to auditors that these were timing issues, not missing information.

On fully depreciated assets, I think a brief note in A6 referencing the treatment in A3 is enough, as long as we have already documented the rationale there. We can mention that these assets remain in use and are monitored operationally, but no further depreciation is recorded.
That works for me. I will double check that A3 clearly shows which assets are fully depreciated and still active, so the note in A6 can simply refer to that schedule.

I will add a short note in A6 on fully depreciated assets, referencing A3 as the detailed source, as you both suggested. That should address any auditor questions without overcomplicating the disclosure.

I have now updated the missing tax references in the relevant T2 templates and confirmed that the associated entries in A6 have complete documentation per A4 and peer review evidence per A7. No further gaps found in the sample I checked.

I have completed the remediation notes in T12 for the open items in A8. Each exception now shows the cause, the fix, and the date resolved. From my side, the compliance review is ready to support the A6 package.

With the additional notes and documentation checks, I am comfortable that A6 reflects the quarter accurately and that we have a solid audit trail via A2, A3, and A8. From a financial statements perspective, I support approving D8 and sending the package to the auditors.
From the documentation and journal side, the checks we did against A4, A7, and A8 give me confidence that the package is ready. I have no remaining concerns and agree with proceeding to D8.
I am aligned as well. The tax notes in A6 match A2 and the compliance log in A8 is up to date with remediation captured in T12. No objections to approving D8.
Confirmed from my side too. The balances in A6 reconcile to the ledger and to A3, and the small points we raised have been addressed. I support D8 and sending the package to the auditors.

Thanks all for the thorough review. With the documentation fixes, updated notes, and compliance remediation in place, I will treat A6 as final for this quarter and proceed to share the package with the external auditor. Recording D8 as approved.
